# A customer and a vendor, both with an address.
#
# The two blocks are the same shape and describe the same kind of thing — who
# the book trades with — and the customer block has carried `addr1:` through
# `email:` all along. The vendor block did not: those keys have no vendor
# setter behind them, so they were filed as custom metadata, which is a slot
# named `addr1` rather than the vendor's address. The export wrote them back
# out of that slot, so the round trip looked clean while the address the book
# actually holds was untouched.
#
# What that costs is visible: `print-bill` renders the vendor's address, and a
# book rebuilt from an export of it renders those lines blank.
#
# Each also carries a key the format has no setter for, kept in a slot beside
# the object. A block that names no such key is not a block asking for the
# slot to be emptied — which is what a printed document carries, and what
# made reading one back a delete.
#
# What this fixture produces: two owners whose addresses come back as
# addresses, and whose extra key survives a printed document.
#
# Verified by tests/integration/test_an_owners_address_survives_a_round_trip.py.
2026-01-01 commodity CAD
	mnemonic: "CAD"
	fullname: "Canadian Dollar"
	namespace: "CURRENCY"
	fraction: 100

customer "C-ADDR"
	name: "Acme Supplies"
	currency: CAD
	addr1: "Acme Supplies Ltd"
	addr2: "1 Front Street"
	addr3: "Toronto ON"
	addr4: "M5J 1A1"
	email: "ap@acme.example"
	department: "north"

vendor "V-ADDR"
	name: "Beta Printing"
	currency: CAD
	addr1: "Beta Printing Inc"
	addr2: "2 Rear Lane"
	addr3: "Hamilton ON"
	addr4: "L8P 1A1"
	email: "invoices@beta.example"
	department: "south"
